title: Horizon and Wreck
premise: Elodie Voss, captain of the riverboat Kestrel, owes a dangerous debt to the Harrow Syndicate and survives by knowing the river better than anyone. When dying prospector Tomas Reyes trades her a map to a lost silver vein for a promise to deliver it to his estranged daughter, Elodie is pulled into a race against the Harrows, who want the map, and against winter, which will seal the mountain pass until the glacier calving season briefly reopens it. Along the way she gathers an unlikely crew—a disgraced surveyor, a runaway telegraph girl, and the daughter herself—and discovers that the 'family' she never wanted is worth more than invisibility ever was. In the end, Elodie burns the map rather than let it buy blood, pays her debt with the truth of what the Harrows did to Tomas, and chooses her found family over the open river she once used to hide.
about_author: Isandro Blackwood is the pen name of a former barge hand turned novelist who spent six seasons working inland waterways before writing full-time. Known for spare prose and river-true detail, Blackwood lives in a converted pilot house with a dog named Sandbar.

chapters.title: The Mood of Water
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A routine run down the Vell River establishes her mastery of sandbars and her careful anonymity—no last name spoken aloud, debts paid in cash. She dodges a Harrow Syndicate toll boat, showing both skill and fear. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Man in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Elodie finds prospector Tomas Reyes half-drowned, shot, and delirious. She hauls him aboard against her instinct to stay uninvolved. He clutches a oilskin packet. POV: Elodie. Beat: compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Price of a Promise
chapters.summary: Tomas offers his map to a lost vein in exchange for one promise: carry it to his daughter Wren in the town of Coldharbor before the passes close. Elodie refuses; he starts dying anyway. POV: Elodie. Beat: guilt taking root.

chapters.title: Harrow Men at the Dock
chapters.summary: Two Syndicate collectors board the Kestrel searching for 'a thief with a packet.' Elodie lies smoothly but realizes they'll be back. POV: Elodie. Beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Carried
chapters.summary: Tomas dies at dawn. Elodie opens the packet: a hand-drawn map keyed to landmarks only a riverwoman could read. POV shifts to a brief interlude from Tomas's final hours. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledgers
chapters.summary: Elodie tries to destroy the map but can't—it's the only thing that could clear her debt if sold, or ruin her if found. She keeps it. POV: Elodie. Beat: the first compromise.

chapters.title: The Surveyor Who Lied
chapters.summary: In Millbrook, Elodie hires Augustin Ferro, a disgraced surveyor who once mapped these ranges, needing his expertise to read the map's high-country notations. He recognizes the terrain instantly—and its danger. POV: Ferro. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: En route upriver, the Kestrel takes on a stowaway: Wren Reyes, seventeen, fleeing Coldharbor after learning her father was alive and looking for her. She doesn't know Elodie carries his map—or his death. POV: Wren. Beat: dramatic irony and ache.

chapters.title: Telegraph Lines and Traplines
chapters.summary: Wren reveals she overheard Harrow agents in Coldharbor planning to intercept 'the Reyes packet' at the pass. Elodie realizes the Syndicate knows more than she thought. POV: alternating. Beat: reluctant alliance formed.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Offer
chapters.summary: Harrow enforcer Corvus Dain corners Elodie at a lock: forgive her entire debt in exchange for the map. She stalls, buying time, heart pounding. POV: Elodie. Beat: temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: Sandbar Justice
chapters.summary: Dain's men try to board at night; Elodie runs the Kestrel through the Widow's Teeth rapids in the dark to lose them, nearly killing everyone. Wren saves Ferro from going overboard. POV: Wren. Beat: trust forged in terror.

chapters.title: Coldharbor
chapters.summary: The crew reaches Coldharbor, Wren's hometown, where old neighbors reveal Tomas left years ago in disgrace—accused of stealing the very claim the map describes. Wren's faith in her father cracks. POV: Wren. Beat: identity shaken.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Choice
chapters.summary: Elodie tells Wren the truth about Tomas's death and the promise. Wren rages, then asks to come the whole way—not for silver, but to learn who her father really was. POV: Wren. Beat: grief converting to purpose.

chapters.title: Ferro's Confession
chapters.summary: Ferro admits he surveyed the Reyes claim years ago and signed the false report that ruined Tomas—the Harrows paid him. He offers this as penance. POV: Ferro. Beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: The Pass Closes Early
chapters.summary: An early storm seals the standard route through the range. The only way forward is the glacier corridor, passable only during calving season when meltwater opens it—for three weeks at most. POV: Elodie. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Provisions and Liars
chapters.summary: Provisioning scene laced with tension: Dain's agents watch the outfitter. Elodie buys gear under false names while Wren charms information out of a clerk about the glacier route's dangers. POV: rotating trio. Beat: crew functioning as one.

chapters.title: The Ascent Begins
chapters.summary: The three leave the Kestrel moored and start up the treeline trail with mules. First night camp: small kindnesses, shared stories, the first feeling of something like family. POV: Ferro. Beat: warmth before the cold.

chapters.title: Treeline
chapters.summary: They find a frozen corpse wearing a Harrow badge—an earlier agent sent after the map, killed by the mountain. Proof Dain's people are ahead of them or behind them. POV: Elodie. Beat: dread.

chapters.title: The Scree Field
chapters.summary: A rockslide separates Wren from the others overnight. She survives alone using her father's old prospecting tricks, taught to her as a child without her understanding why. POV: Wren. Beat: legacy revealed as love.

chapters.title: Dain on the Trail
chapters.summary: Corvus Dain catches up, alone, offering again: the debt forgiven, plus Wren's safety guaranteed, for the map. Elodie nearly accepts—until Dain lets slip that the Harrows murdered Tomas. POV: Elodie. Beat: the deal dies.

chapters.title: Blood on the Moraine
chapters.summary: Violent standoff on the moraine; Ferro takes a bullet meant for Elodie. They drive Dain off but he escapes with one of their mules and supplies. POV: Ferro, fading in and out. Beat: sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Storm-bound in a cave for four days, low on food. Ferro feverish. Wren and Elodie keep him alive by turns, talking through the night—first real conversation between them. POV: Wren. Beat: intimacy born of crisis.

chapters.title: What Elodie Owes
chapters.summary: Elodie finally tells the full story of her debt: she took the fall for a Harrow smuggling run captained by the man she loved, who abandoned her to it. Wren sees her clearly for the first time. POV: Elodie. Beat: vulnerability as turning point.

chapters.title: The Glacier's Mouth
chapters.summary: They reach the ice corridor just as calving season opens—thunderous, beautiful, terrifying. The route is open but won't stay so. POV: Elodie. Beat: awe and urgency.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Crossing the glacier, a massive calving splits their path; they must cross a widening crevasse field on a shrinking schedule. Ferro, still weak, insists he can make it. POV: Ferro. Beat: courage against the body's limits.

chapters.title: The Blue Cathedral
chapters.summary: Inside the ice, a moment of grace: light through blue walls, the three of them laughing for the first time. Brief peace before the endgame. POV: Wren. Beat: joy earned.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Far Side
chapters.summary: Dain and six Harrow men wait at the glacier's exit—they've taken the low route. Outnumbered, outgunned, cornered against the ice. POV: Elodie. Beat: trap sprung.

chapters.title: The Map Is Not the Treasure
chapters.summary: Under threat, Elodie understands what Tomas truly meant: the map's landmarks describe not just silver but evidence—the Harrows' forged claim documents hidden in the same cache, proof that would break the Syndicate. POV: Elodie. Beat: revelation reframes everything.

chapters.title: Standoff on the Ice
chapters.summary: Negotiation turns violent. Wren, using her father's knowledge of the glacier, triggers a controlled calving that scatters the Harrow men. Dain grabs Elodie; she breaks free at cost of a gashed arm. POV: Wren. Beat: the student becomes the fighter.

chapters.title: The Cache
chapters.summary: They reach the site: silver enough to matter, and the iron box of documents proving the Harrows stole the Reyes claim and killed to protect the lie. Wren holds her father's vindication in her hands. POV: Wren. Beat: truth unearthed.

chapters.title: Dain's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Wounded Dain returns alone, desperate. He offers everything one final time. Elodie refuses—not with anger but with pity—and lets the mountain decide his fate as he retreats onto unstable ice. POV: Elodie. Beat: mercy and consequence.

chapters.title: Descent Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: The race down: weather turning, Ferro worsening, the window closing. They push through the night, carrying each other literally at points. POV: rotating. Beat: endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: The River Again
chapters.summary: They reach the Kestrel as first snow falls. Ferro needs a doctor; the nearest one is in Harrow-controlled territory. Elodie must sail straight into the wolf's mouth. POV: Elodie. Beat: courage redirected.

chapters.title: Into Harrow Waters
chapters.summary: Elodie runs the Syndicate blockade using every trick the river ever taught her, ferrying the documents toward the federal assayer's office in Vellport. POV: Elodie. Beat: all skills converging.

chapters.title: The Assayer's Office
chapters.summary: Documents delivered; the assayer wires territorial marshals. But Dain survived and has wired ahead too—Elodie is named as a claim-jumper and thief. Warrant issued. POV: Wren. Beat: victory poisoned.

chapters.title: Trial by Testimony
chapters.summary: In Vellport, Wren testifies about her father; Ferro confesses his false report publicly, ruining himself to save them. The marshals arrest Dain instead. Elodie's debt is voided by the Syndicate's collapse—but her name is only cleared because friends told the truth for her. POV: Ferro. Beat: loyalty outweighing truth's cost.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the Reyes claim legally restored to Wren. She offers Elodie a partnership; Elodie, terrified of being anchored, almost flees. POV: Elodie. Beat: the choice between hiding and belonging.

chapters.title: The Compass Pointed Home
chapters.summary: Elodie unpacks the meaning of her compass—her father's, which she'd followed away from every harbor. She realizes it always pointed wherever she refused to go. She stays. POV: Elodie. Beat: identity resolved.

chapters.title: Launch Season
chapters.summary: Spring on the Vell. The Kestrel refitted, now flying the Reyes-Voss line. Ferro recovers as the outfit's surveyor; Wren runs the books. Small domestic joys rendered in river detail. POV: Wren. Beat: found family made ordinary and real.

chapters.title: Horizon and Wreck
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Elodie's POV, mirroring chapter one: the same run, the same sandbars—but now she answers to her full name, waves at familiar docks, and carries passengers instead of secrets. On the horizon, mountains where a promise was kept. Beat: arrival, not escape—the wreck behind her, the horizon ahead, and home in both directions.
